record_type_quote: Participants with OCD and matched control participants wrote about an immoral deed they had committed, after which half of the participants in each group cleaned their hands with a wipe.

targets.title: Washing away your sins: Threatened morality and physical cleansing.
targets.evidence_quote: In this study we borrowed the procedure used by Zhong and Liljenquist (2006) to examine the relationship between cleanliness and morality in OCD. Replicating Zhong and Liljenquist, we found that cleaning hands after writing about an immoral deed reduced participants’ willingness to help another person.
targets.outcome_quote: Replicating previous findings, physical cleaning reduced the willingness to help and relieved moral emotions.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly confirm both tested effects; OCD amplification is an extension.

reasoning: A new OCD and matched control sample re-tests the published cleansing effects. The other cited studies motivate or contextualize the work rather than being targets.
